tagline: A 715 KB ternary decision model that plays four games at the oracle's level and answers typed questions in free text, above the majority class of the typed-decisions bench.
short_description: 715 KB model for four games and typed questions
notes: Published at full depth: its conformal early-exit thresholds were rejected by the pre-registered arena check.
0.480 on the typed-decisions bench, where the majority class is 0.398 and s5-lite reaches 0.696: expect mistakes on questions in free text.

It passed its gate, but a constant answer per task passes it too: answering each question with its most common training answer scores 0.4815 on the bench, and on 17 of the 20 bench tasks s6-nano gives one answer to at least 95% of the items (docs/s6-nano2-study.md).

tagline: A 2.4 MB ternary decision model that plays four games at the oracle's level and answers typed questions in free text: 0.553 on the typed-decisions bench. Its second version passed the gate that the first one failed, on the same test records.
short_description: 2.4 MB model for four games and typed questions
notes: A second look: the first version (s6-micro-v1) failed the ECE guard at 0.0821 against 0.08. This version was designed after that reading (twice the decision-training minutes) and judged on the same test records: 0.553 on the bench (gate 0.45), ECE 0.0588, every game at s3-pico's score (docs/s6-gen-prereg.md, amendment 17).
Published at full depth: its conformal early-exit thresholds were rejected by the pre-registered arena check (one extra Dodge veto).

Expect mistakes on questions in free text: 0.401 on When2Call, where it rarely chooses to call a tool, and 0.092 on NOTAM subjects. On 11 of the 20 bench tasks it gives one answer to at least 95% of the items.

tagline: A 250 KB ternary secret detector that passes its pre-registered gate on a synthetic bench and fails on real files: published as a result, not as a scanner.
short_description: 250 KB secrets model: a result, not a scanner
notes: On a synthetic bench of file types it never saw, it beats a gitleaks-style rule scanner: secret 0.9990 against 0.977, service 0.9795 against 0.787. The bench comes from our own generator.

On real files it fails: on 719 source, configuration and documentation files with no secret, it flags 59.8% of the files at p ≥ 0.9 and 49.4% at p ≥ 0.999 (github.com/maxgfr/secretgate/pull/19). Do not use it to scan real files.
The line answer is weak (0.6859 on the bench): do not rely on it.

The presets are texts of the generator's bench, and their keys are fake, generated in each provider's public format with a random body. Everything runs in your browser: nothing you paste is sent anywhere.

tagline: Failed its pre-registered gate, published as a result: a 2.4 MB ternary model for four games and typed questions, 0.547 on the typed-decisions bench but ECE 0.0821 against a guard of 0.08.
short_description: Failed its gate: 2.4 MB s6 model, a result
notes: The gate (docs/s6-gen-prereg.md §6): at least 0.45 on the typed-decisions bench, ECE at most 0.08, no game more than 5% below s3-pico. It reached 0.547 and plays every game at s3-pico's score, but its ECE is 0.0821 at full depth: it failed, and is recommended for no use.

Published at full depth (its three exit thresholds set to 1). Its four-times-smaller sibling s6-nano passed the same gate, and so did the second version, s6-micro, on a second look at the same test records.
Expect mistakes on questions in free text: 0.430 on When2Call, 0.052 on NOTAM subjects.

tagline: Failed three of its four pre-registered gates, published as a result: a 899 KB ternary model that hears the last 10 s of audio and answers typed questions about it.
short_description: Failed its gates: 899 KB audio model, a result
notes: End of turn 0.5681 against 0.9263 for Smart Turn v3.2 on the same clips (fail; Pipecat's report; the v1 harness read 0.8518); 12 Speech Commands keywords 0.8885 against 0.90 (fail); zero-shot keywords 0.2100 in English (pass, bar 0.20) and 0.1330 in French (fail).
Its control, trained the same way without the Mimi pretraining, is more accurate on all four sets: the pretraining did not help in this run. The control is not published.
The demo answers at full depth, where the gates were read; the file keeps the exit thresholds its training run stored (choice 0.5, score 0.9, noul 0.68).

tagline: Failed its pre-registered gate, published as a result: a 143 KB ternary forecaster (nine deciles) that scores nGMASE 0.9471 and nWQL 0.6646 on GIFT-Eval, where the gate asked for 0.838 and 0.587.
short_description: Failed its gate: 143 KB forecaster, a result
notes: The gate was to beat the training-free FLAIR on GIFT-Eval (nGMASE ≤ 0.838 and nWQL ≤ 0.587), with the goal of beating TinyCast (0.774 / 0.545). It met neither, with or without flip (0.9099 / 0.6417 with flip).
It beats the seasonal naive on WQL in 84 of 97 configurations, but on MASE only in 52; on MASE, medium and long horizons are worse than the seasonal naive.
s6-cast-pico starts unticked: tick it to compare it with TinyCast and the seasonal naive on the same series.

tagline: A 17M-parameter decision model whose options cannot see each other: reordering the options or renaming their keys cannot change an answer.
short_description: 17M decision model, invariant to option order and keys
notes: This checkpoint is a longer run (8,000 steps) added for the demo outside the pre-registered bets; see the results page for what failed and why.
It answers 21 of the 30 English demo cases: expect mistakes, especially on incidents and severity.
